Roboai ( (AIIO) ) has provided an update.

On August 20, 2026, Robo.ai Inc. reported that it has completed a sweeping restructuring, disposing of legacy operations that carried most of its historical liabilities and repositioning itself around newly acquired AI and deep‑tech assets. The company will publish unaudited results for the six months ended June 30, 2026 on August 24, 2026, cautioning that the period reflects a business in transition and is not comparable with 2025.

During the first half of 2026, Robo.ai acquired Neurovia AI, gaining exclusive rights to AI data processing and compression technologies now being tested with customers in sectors such as public safety, transportation, energy and municipal services. It also bought Quantum Core Capital, an AI‑driven deep‑tech holding and venture‑building platform expected to ramp up operations in the UAE, signaling a push into incubation and investment alongside operating businesses.

The group further established Alif Holding, an industrial arm focused on technology infrastructure and advanced materials for government, public sector and other mission‑critical domains in the UAE. Governance at Alif has been reinforced by appointing former INTERPOL president Dr. Ahmed Naser Al‑Raisi as chairman and former UAE Ministry of Interior official Dr. Jasem Al‑Mansory as chief executive, underscoring Robo.ai’s bid to anchor itself as a strategically important player in regional intelligent infrastructure.

Management said the divestiture of the legacy business and these acquisitions are expected to move shareholders’ equity into positive territory and lay the groundwork for improved revenue and profitability over time. For investors, the shift marks an inflection point, with near‑term financials likely to remain volatile as integration, commercialization and supply‑chain build‑out progress, but with the balance sheet strengthened and a clearer focus on high‑value AI, industrial and digital asset platforms.

More about Roboai

Robo.ai Inc. is a technology group focused on building intelligent infrastructure across four platforms: artificial intelligence, robotics and smart mobility, advanced manufacturing, and digital assets and capital. Through Alif Holding, Neurovia AI and Quantum Core Capital, it develops and manufactures AI systems and visual data infrastructure, and incubates deep‑tech ventures serving government, public sector and mission‑critical domains from its Abu Dhabi headquarters.
